parsed.corrected_rationale: The comment refers to "the prompt templates used in the paper," but only in a general way, without pointing to any specific section, table, figure, or experiment. The authors would have to make an educated guess about which part of the paper is being addressed, since the comment does not indicate where the simple templates appear. On the specificity side, the comment does detail the issue (the templates are simple) and provides concrete examples of more effective prompting methods (Chain-of-Thought and Least-to-Most prompting) with citations, so it clearly specifies what could be improved. However, because the referenced part cannot be confidently pinpointed by the authors, the comment does not meet the requirements for a fully grounded and specific comment under the rubric's highest level.
